subject: other-disciplines
audience: FE Other Disciplines candidates and engineering students
title: The Confined Space That Needed 18 m³/min, Not 1,080
featured_title: THE CONFINED SPACE THAT NEEDED 18 CUBIC METERS PER MINUTE NOT 1080

presentation.challenge: Six air changes per hour sounded like 1,080 m³/min when the hour-to-minute conversion was skipped. The required flow was 18 m³/min.

practice.primary_question: How is ventilation flow rate calculated from enclosure volume and required air changes per hour?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Multiplying enclosure volume by air changes per hour and reporting the result directly in m³/min without dividing by 60.

case_dna.target_misconception: A 180 m³ space requiring 6 air changes per hour needs 180×6=1080 m³/min of ventilation.
case_dna.why_plausible: The volume-times-air-change calculation is correct in m³/hour, but the time unit is easy to mislabel.
case_dna.corrected_model: For ACH in h^-1, Q=V×ACH gives volume per hour. Divide by 60 to express the result in m³/min.

problem_statement: A confined space has a volume of 180 m³. A ventilation plan specifies 6 air changes per hour. A note multiplies 180×6=1080 and reports 1080 m³/min. Determine the correct required ventilation flow in m³/min and the corresponding nominal air-replacement time.
fixed_constraints: Assume perfectly distributed ventilation for the ACH calculation

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The arithmetic was correct. The time unit was not.
gates.prompt: What conversion is needed to express flow in m³/min?

options.label: Use Q=V×ACH/60 for m³/min
options.reason: V×ACH gives m³/hour, so dividing by 60 converts to m³/min.

options.label: Use Q=V×ACH directly as m³/min
options.reason: That mislabels an hourly volumetric rate as a per-minute rate.

options.label: Use Q=V/ACH
options.reason: That has units of m³·h and is not the ventilation flow relation.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the required ventilation flow
gates.prompt: Enter the flow rate in m³/min.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Convert ACH into volumetric flow
gates.result: The required ventilation flow is 18 m³/min.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the ventilation flow
gates.hint: Six air changes per hour means six room volumes per hour.

cards.text: Nominal replacement time=180/18=10 min, which is also 60/6=10 min per air change.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the ventilation note
report: C1. The space volume is 180 m³.
C2. Six air changes per hour require 1080 m³ each hour.
C3. Therefore the required flow is 1080 m³/min.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This hourly exchange volume is correct.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It fails to convert the hourly rate to a per-minute flow.

evidence_choices.label: 1080 m³/h ÷ 60=18 m³/min
evidence_choices.reason: This is the required unit conversion.

correction.template: The required ventilation flow is {flow} m³/min, corresponding to {replacement_time} min per nominal air change.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Increase the ventilation requirement to 8 ACH
gates.constraint: Keep the space volume at 180 m³.

options.label: Use 1,440 m³/min
options.reason: That again treats the hourly exchange volume as a per-minute flow.

options.label: Use 13.5 m³/min
options.reason: That would correspond to only 4.5 ACH.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply ACH to another enclosure
gates.prompt: A 300 m³ enclosure requires 4 ACH. What flow is required in m³/min?

options.label: 1,200 m³/min
options.reason: That is the hourly exchange volume mislabeled per minute.

options.label: 75 m³/min
options.reason: That does not match the ACH conversion.

gates.explanation: Convert the hourly air-change requirement into a per-minute volumetric flow.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the ventilation calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that ACH is an hourly frequency and that ventilation flow must use consistent time units.

items.label: What failed
items.value: An hourly volumetric rate was mislabeled as a per-minute rate.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use Q=V×ACH/60 when Q is required in m³/min.

seo.seo_title: Confined Space Ventilation From Air Changes per Hour | FE E-091
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Other Disciplines Case E-091: a 180 m³ space at 6 ACH needs 18 m³/min of ventilation, not 1,080 m³/min.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE confined space ventilation air changes per hour
seo.excerpt: Air changes per hour produce an hourly volumetric rate. Convert that rate before reporting ventilation in m³/min.
seo.direct_answer: For a 180 m³ space at 6 ACH, Q=180×6=1080 m³/h=18 m³/min. One nominal air change therefore takes 10 minutes.

faqs.q: How do you convert ACH to ventilation flow?
faqs.a: Use Q=V×ACH, then convert the resulting time unit as needed.
